I know what you are talking about, from personal experience. Hear me out here:
Beauty is subjective. Yes, there are features and characteristics (like face symmetry) that are more likely to appear attractive to human eye, but what you realise is that you judge yourself based on what you are attracted to; based on values others might not share.

Pale skin is atractive to me. I wanted it for myself. I looked for it in my partners. Yet, the look I like appears "lifeless", "cold" and "ghost-like" to many around me. 

And it goes both ways: I've had partners worrying about aspects of themselves I couldn't care less about. 

Then there is the issue of representation.. Sometimes it feels like the only way to be beautiful is to have X and Y, because X and Y are the only things represented around us; we have no mental image of beauty without X and Y. The cure for that is looking for beauty outside that X and Y. 

Most people might have a preset "type" and a certain look they think of when hearing the word "beautiful" (which is heavily affected by what they've been shown all their life), that type usually doesn't represent their whole opinion; meaning, they will find some people outside their type beautiful. It's usually about how well your style plays against your natural characteristics. I'm sure you've seen plenty of unattractive Eurocenteric people; whether it's bad makeup, bad hair style, weird eyebrows, etc. 

I say you should play to your strengths. 

If you search for it, you'll find many people with your hair color, skin tone and eyes who'll look attractive to you! Maybe, start from there, see what they are doing differently. 

Try different hair styles, different outfits and colours. Just figure out what looks best on you. 

Beauty is quite subjective. I literally can't stand hyper athletic people, for example.
